elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — covers both the Agreement and any Order Form, unconditional election, so a true convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — exactly 30 days, in writing, and no additional conditions or approval requirements attach.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination" — the words "pro rata" are express, not merely inferred from a post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term." Retained Sections 9.1–9.3 give Vendor only cause- and insolvency-based exits, so nothing contradicts this.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause sets 30 days, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (and better than it); the fallback band is literally not satisfied.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-payment mechanic is imposed anywhere in Section 9 or the inserted clause, so there is no fee to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply in a stricter form: Vendor is expressly given no convenience right at all during a committed term, which is more restrictive than a term-end-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor holds no convenience termination right under the amended Section 9, so no notice period is needed.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met by the single inserted paragraph — 30 days' written notice, Agreement or Order Form scope, express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
Fallback is not independently complete only because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90; that is a Customer-favourable overshoot and irrelevant given the preferred level is met.

Minimal: the drafter correctly dropped the model language's surplus "in whole or in part" (no partial-termination structure in the cited Order Form provisions requires it) and added no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, or extra remedy. No existing words were deleted; Sections 9.1, 9.2, 9.3 and 9.5 survive verbatim, and Section 8.2's 180-day non-renewal notice is correctly left alone as a RENEWAL matter rather than double-flagged here.

Preserves intent: the new right is additive and consistent with retained Section 9.5 ("A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy"), and Section 8.1's "unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms" already contemplates earlier termination, so no contradictory retained sentence or dangling cross-reference results.

Drafting nit only (does not affect the operative result): the inserted paragraph is rendered without its "9.4" number even though the comment calls it a new 9.4; number the clause on execution so the sequence 9.3 / 9.4 / 9.5 is clean. No cross-reference elsewhere depends on it.
